title: Picard group of an affine curve as a Jacobian quotient
statement: Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ ([def-sc-curves]), let $\overline C$ be a smooth proper connected curve over $k$ with an open immersion $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ whose complement $S:=\overline C\setminus C$ is a finite set of closed points ([lem-sc-compactification]), and let $J$ be a Jacobian of $\overline C$ ([def-sc-jacobian], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]), with the canonical identification $J(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$. Then $S$ is nonempty, and for every point $P_0\in S$ and the subgroup $\Lambda:=\langle [P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\subseteq J(k)$ (classes taken under that identification) there is a group isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong J(k)/\Lambda$.

proof.text: The boundary $S$ is nonempty. If $S$ were empty, then $C=\overline C$ would be both proper and affine over $k$, so [lem-sc-proper-affine-finite] would make it finite over $k$, hence of dimension zero, contradicting that a connected curve has dimension one ([def-sc-curves]).

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, nonemptiness of S

proof.text: By [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve], for each of the smooth connected curves $C$ and $\overline C$ the map $D\mapsto[\mathcal O(D)]$ identifies $\operatorname{Cl}$ with $\operatorname{Pic}$, compatibly with restriction to the open $C\subseteq\overline C$. Restriction of divisors $\operatorname{Div}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Div}(C)$ (forget the coefficients at the points of $S$) is surjective (extend by coefficient zero on $S$), and its kernel is the free subgroup $\bigoplus_{P\in S}\mathbf Z\,P$. Since $C$ is dense open in the integral curve $\overline C$, both have the same function field $K$, and $\operatorname{div}_{\overline C}(f)$ restricts to $\operatorname{div}_C(f)$ for $f\in K^\times$; so restriction maps principal divisors onto principal divisors, and a divisor on $\overline C$ whose restriction is $\operatorname{div}_C(f)$ differs from $\operatorname{div}_{\overline C}(f)$ by a divisor supported on $S$. Hence $\bigoplus_{P\in S}\mathbf Z\to\operatorname{Cl}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Cl}(C)\to0$ is exact, i.e. $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)/B$ with $B:=\langle[P]:P\in S\rangle$, $[P]=[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P)]$ (Hartshorne II.6.5).

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: By [lem-sc-pic-proper-decomposition], $\deg:\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)\to\mathbf Z$ is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$. Fix $P_0\in S$ (possible by step 1); $\deg[P_0]=1$. The map $r:\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$, $x\mapsto x-\deg(x)[P_0]$, is a homomorphism that is the identity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$, so it is surjective with kernel $\mathbf Z[P_0]$. Since $[P]=[P_0]+([P]-[P_0])$ for $P\in S$, we have $B=\mathbf Z[P_0]+\Lambda_0$ with $\Lambda_0:=\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$, and $r(B)=\Lambda_0$; as $\ker r\subseteq B$, $r$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)/B\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\Lambda_0$. With step 2, $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\Lambda_0$.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, splitting by P0

proof.text: By the canonical identification $J(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$ of the statement ([def-sc-jacobian], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]), a group isomorphism, $\Lambda_0$ corresponds to $\Lambda=\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\subseteq J(k)$, and step 3 becomes the group isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong J(k)/\Lambda$.

lean.statement: theorem IsConnectedCurve.pic_affine_quotient {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C] (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [Smooth c.g] [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] [GeometricallyIntegral c.g] (hfin : (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ.Finite) (hcl : ∀ x ∈ (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ, IsClosed ({x} : Set c.Z)) (J : Over (Spec (.of k))) [CommGrpObj J] [IsJacobian c.g J] (G : Subgroup c.Z.Pic) (hG : (G : Set c.Z.Pic) = c.g.picZero) (e : G ≃* (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ J)) : (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ.Nonempty ∧ ∀ (P₀ : closedPoints c.Z), P₀.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base → Nonempty (Additive C.Pic ≃+ Additive (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ J) ⧸ AddSubgroup.closure {a | ∃ (P : closedPoints c.Z) (L : G), P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧ L.val = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P / @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P₀ ∧ a = Additive.ofMul (e L)})
